self_report_summary: The user describes difficulty focusing consistently.
behavioral_summary: Conversation behavior shows frequent topic switching alongside sustained, detailed engagement when a topic becomes personally meaningful.

dimensions.name: attentional_switching
dimensions.evidence_summary: Topics change frequently across exploratory exchanges.
dimensions.counter_evidence: Long threads sometimes remain tightly scoped.

dimensions.name: focus_persistence
dimensions.evidence_summary: Once engaged, the user sustains detailed multi-step work.
dimensions.counter_evidence: Routine topics are sometimes left quickly.

dimensions.name: associative_branching
dimensions.evidence_summary: One question often opens several related lines of inquiry.
dimensions.counter_evidence: The user can request a narrow response when needed.

dimensions.name: disengagement_difficulty
dimensions.evidence_summary: Deeply engaging topics sometimes continue beyond the initial task.
dimensions.counter_evidence: Explicit stopping points are usually followed.

dimensions.name: novelty_dependence
dimensions.evidence_summary: New angles appear to renew engagement.
dimensions.counter_evidence: Some repetitive refinement work is sustained.

dimensions.name: emotional_capture
dimensions.evidence_summary: Emotional material sometimes redirects the discussion.

dimensions.name: energy_dullness
dimensions.evidence_summary: Long engaged exchanges do not usually show fading alertness.
dimensions.counter_evidence: Conversation timing cannot reliably show physical energy.

dimensions.name: low_stimulation_tolerance
dimensions.evidence_summary: There is mixed evidence about remaining with low-stimulation tasks.

dimensions.name: metacognitive_noticing
dimensions.evidence_summary: The user often notices and corrects the direction of an exchange.
dimensions.counter_evidence: Some shifts are recognized only after several turns.

dimensions.name: sensory_orientation
dimensions.evidence_summary: Verbal and conceptual cues are more visible than sensory cues in conversation.
dimensions.counter_evidence: Conversation is a poor setting for observing sensory orientation.

key_disagreements: The self-description of weak focus conflicts with sustained engagement during personally meaningful work.

alternative_interpretations.label: Generalized weak concentration
alternative_interpretations.reason: Possible, but it does not explain repeated periods of sustained detailed engagement.

alternative_interpretations.label: Context-sensitive engagement
alternative_interpretations.reason: Interest and task meaning may strongly affect whether attention settles.

limitations: Conversation behavior reflects only one setting.
No clinical or diagnostic inference is warranted.
